# 2d Cut-off, Phase 2 exit: contract

**Read first:** [build README → Phase 2](./README.md#phase-2-subscriptions), [credential rotation](../processes/servers/credential-rotation.md) (all, especially "cut-off"), [link lifecycle](../processes/subscriptions/link-lifecycle.md) (Cut off), [subscriptions module → Disabling is not revoking](../modules/subscriptions.md#disabling-is-not-revoking), [server redeploy → rolling upgrade](../processes/servers/server-redeploy.md) (the pattern: no job waits for another, a subscriber starts the next), [roadmap → Phase 2 exit](../roadmap.md#phase-2-subscriptions), [open questions](../open-questions.md) ("to verify" 1 and 2), the **As built** of 2a–2c and of 1e (rotation, the rollout subscriber in `servers/deploy/rollout.go`).

**Done when:** **Cut off** on a link shows what will happen, disables the link at once and rotates every server of its subscription one at a time, the link page follows the rotations and offers **Retry** for a server whose rotation failed; the servers module offers rotation as a port; the gateway's access log no longer records link tokens (drafted for the user); the Phase 2 exit demo is written down for the user; every checklist line has its test.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Port | New in servers: `type Rotator interface { RotationRequest(ctx, serverID int64, actor string) (jobs.Request, error) }`, `func (m *Module) Rotator() Rotator`, and `servers.ErrNotActive = deploy.ErrNotActive`, `servers.ErrNothingToRotate = deploy.ErrNothingToRotate`. `deploy.Service.RotationRequest` checks the server is active and not retiring and has rotatable values (as `Rotate` does now) and returns the `servers.rotate` request (payload, resource key `server:<id>`, `CreatedBy: actor`) without enqueuing it; `Rotate` becomes `RotationRequest` + `EnqueueNow`, unchanged for its callers. `main.go` wires `Rotator: srv.Rotator()`. | The caller enqueues inside its own transaction: the link is disabled and the first rotation queued together, or neither. |
| Plan | `GET /links/:id/cutoff`, a page styled as a strength-2 dialog: "Cut off Alex". It says the link is disabled at once; lists the subscription's members in order, each with its health or why it can't be rotated ("not in service", "its template has no rotatable values"; asked with `RotationRequest`, nothing enqueued); counts the other links that will get new URIs ("10 other links in 3 subscriptions get new URIs on their next refresh": active, unexpired links other than this one whose subscription holds any server that will rotate); and repeats rotation's warning ("Apps refresh within their update interval (12 h by default). Until an app refreshes, it can't connect to a rotated server. Anyone using a copied URI or a disabled link loses access."). A subscription with nothing to rotate: "Nothing to rotate: Cut off only disables the link." A deleted link → 409. Without a `Rotator` the action is hidden everywhere. | credential-rotation.md cut-off step 1; ui/README "consequence texts are concrete". |
| Start | `POST /links/:id/cutoff`, one `Write`: the link → disabled when it is active (`link.disabled`); a `subs_cutoffs` row and one item per member in subscription order (`waiting`); `advance`; `link.cut_off{servers, skipped}` (names of the servers it will rotate and of those it skipped). `Jobs.Kick()` after the commit. → the link page. | credential-rotation.md cut-off step 2: the link at once, then the rotations. |
| One at a time | `advance(ctx, tx, cutoffID, actor)`: when no item of the cut-off is `running`, take the first `waiting` item by position and ask `RotationRequest`; `ErrNotActive` → `skipped` "not in service", `ErrNothingToRotate` → `skipped` "no rotatable values", and go on to the next; a request → `Jobs.Enqueue(ctx, tx, req)` in the same transaction → `running` with its `job_id`. Any other error is returned (the transaction rolls back; a subscriber's delivery is retried). The unique index lets at most one item run. | Build README default; the docs' "one server at a time". |
| Subscriber | `subscriptions.cutoff`, types `server.credentials_rotated` and `server.redeploy_failed`. The job id comes from the event's actor (`job:<id>`; anything else → ignore). The item `running` with that `job_id` (none → ignore: already handled, or not a cut-off's rotation) becomes `done` on `server.credentials_rotated`, or `failed` on `server.redeploy_failed` with `kind: rotate` and its `error` (`"cancelled"` when `cancelled: true`); then `advance` with actor `event:<id>`. A failure doesn't stop the chain. Every way a rotation job ends records one of the two events (1e: success, failure, cancel — queued or running), so the chain never stalls. | 1e rollout subscriber; credential-rotation.md edge case "server 3 still runs". |
| Retry | `POST /links/:id/cutoff/:position/retry` for a `failed` item: back to `waiting` (job and error cleared), then `advance` (it starts at once when nothing runs, else after the running one). No event of its own: the rotation records its own. Skipped items have no Retry. | credential-rotation.md rules "each with Retry". |
| Progress | The link page shows the **latest** cut-off of the link in a **Cut-off** area: when it started and by whom; per server: waiting / rotating (link to the job) / rotated / "failed: <error> · still has the old credential" with **Retry** / "skipped: <reason> · still has the old credential". While an item waits or runs, the area polls `GET /links/:id/cutoff/status` every 2 s (`hx-trigger="every 2s"`), and the answer drops the trigger once nothing waits or runs. | credential-rotation.md cut-off step 3: "the link page shows their progress". |
| Band | 2c's alert band gains **Cut off Alex…** with "Disables the link and rotates nl-1 and se-1, so copied URIs stop working too." The **Actions** area gains **Cut off…** too. | `RP-Link`. |
| Cut-off of a disabled link | Allowed: no `link.disabled`, rotations as usual. A second cut-off while one runs: allowed; each has its own items, the page shows the newest; rotations of one server queue behind each other on its resource key. | |
| Gateway log | Draft, as an **uncommitted** change in `~/projects/sh-main/nginx/conf.d/proxier.conf` for the user (like 0e's drafts): a `map $uri $proxier_log { ~^/(s\|r\|f)/ 0; default 1; }` above the server block and `access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log json if=$proxier_log;` inside it, so the gateway stops writing tokens into its JSON access log (`$uri` is logged as `http_path`). Say so in `docs/deployment.md`. | Proxier masks its own log (2b); the gateway logs every path. |

## Go signatures

```go
package servers
type Rotator interface {
	// RotationRequest is the job that rotates the server, for the caller to
	// enqueue in its own transaction. ErrNotActive: not active, or retiring.
	// ErrNothingToRotate: its version marks no generated value rotate: true.
	RotationRequest(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, actor string) (jobs.Request, error)
}
var (
	ErrNotActive       = deploy.ErrNotActive
	ErrNothingToRotate = deploy.ErrNothingToRotate
)
func (m *Module) Rotator() Rotator

package deploy
func (s *Service) RotationRequest(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, actor string) (jobs.Request, error)

package links
type CutOffPlan struct {
	Link       Link
	Rotate     []PlanServer // in subscription order
	Skip       []PlanServer // with Reason
	OtherLinks int
	OtherSubs  int
}
type PlanServer struct {
	ServerID       int64
	Name, Health   string
	Reason         string // skipped only: "not in service", "no rotatable values"
}
type CutOff struct {
	ID        int64
	CreatedAt time.Time
	CreatedBy string
	Items     []CutOffItem
}
type CutOffItem struct {
	Position   int
	ServerID   int64
	ServerName string
	State      string // waiting, running, done, failed, skipped
	JobID      int64
	Error      string
}
func (s *Service) PlanCutOff(ctx context.Context, linkID int64) (CutOffPlan, error)
func (s *Service) CutOff(ctx context.Context, linkID int64, actor string) (cutoffID int64, err error)
func (s *Service) RetryCutOff(ctx context.Context, linkID int64, position int, actor string) error
func (s *Service) LatestCutOff(ctx context.Context, linkID int64) (CutOff, bool, error)
func (s *Service) CutOffSubscriber() events.Subscriber // "subscriptions.cutoff"

package substest
// Rotator is a fake servers.Rotator: it answers requests of the fake job type
// "fake.rotate" (registered by the harness; no worker runs it), or the error a
// test set for a server.
type Rotator struct{ /* … */ }
func (r *Rotator) Refuse(serverID int64, err error)
// Rotated and RotationFailed feed the cut-off subscriber (inside a Write) the
// event a real rotation would record for the job: actor "job:<jobID>",
// subject "server:<serverID>", payload kind "rotate" for a failure.
func (h *Harness) Rotated(jobID, serverID int64)
func (h *Harness) RotationFailed(jobID, serverID int64, msg string)
```

## Routes

| Method, path | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /links/:id/cutoff` | The plan |
| `POST /links/:id/cutoff` | Start → the link page |
| `GET /links/:id/cutoff/status` | The Cut-off area (polling) |
| `POST /links/:id/cutoff/:position/retry` | Retry one server |

## Events

Recorded: `link.disabled` (when it was active), `link.cut_off{servers, skipped}`. The rotations record `server.credentials_rotated` and `server.redeploy_failed` themselves.

## Phase 2 exit demo

The user runs it on `proxier.tikhonnnnn.com` with at least one active server; Claude writes down the steps and fills in **As built** from what the user reports, never pretending to have run them:

1. Subscriptions → **New subscription** "Me" with the server; another, "Family", with it too.
2. **New link** "Tikhon — iPhone" in Me → on the phone, add the subscription by scanning the QR (Happ, Streisand or v2RayTun). The app shows the title and the server, connects, and refreshes. Note which headers it honours (title, interval, expiry) — open question "to verify" 2.
3. **New link** for a family member in Family; their phone imports it and connects.
4. **Disable…** the family link → refresh in their app → its list becomes the single entry "⛔ Ссылка отключена · пишите …" (or the English one); **Enable** → the server comes back on the next refresh. Note which apps replace their list and which keep the old one — open question "to verify" 1.
5. Fetch one link from more than 4 networks within a day (the phone on mobile data and on Wi-Fi, `curl` through a few VPN exits) → within 15 minutes a 🟡 "… looks shared" message in Telegram, and the band on the link page.
6. Optional: **Cut off** a test link of a subscription → the rotations run one by one; the other link's app works again after a refresh; the cut-off link's copied URI no longer connects.
7. Record what passed in As built; answer open questions 1 and 2 in `docs/open-questions.md`; set the roadmap's Phase 2 line; add the DONE entry to `CLAUDE.md`.

## As built

Built 2026-10-08. Every automated checklist line has its test, in the file the line names. `make check` (exit 0), `make lint` (0 issues) and `docker build .` are green; every package of the module runs under `-race`, the two real-servers cut-off tests included. The three manual lines are the user's and are **not done**: the Phase 2 exit demo, open questions "to verify" 1 and 2 (left open in `docs/open-questions.md`), and committing and deploying the gateway draft. The pages were also opened in a real Chrome (headless, puppeteer-core, a throwaway site seeded from `substest`; nothing committed): the plan page, the link page's Cut-off area (failed with Retry, rotating with its job, waiting) and the alert band's **Cut off Dad…** at 1280 and 390 px, no horizontal scroll, no console error or CSP violation, and the area polled `…/cutoff/status` every 2 s while a rotation ran. Deviations and notes:

- **Port.** `servers.Rotator` / `Module.Rotator()` as contracted; the port also maps a server that doesn't exist (`store.ErrNotFound`) to `ErrNotActive`, so a cut-off never fails on a server deleted from under it. `deploy.Service.Rotate` is now `RotationRequest` + `EnqueueNow`.
- **Skipping happens at Cut off.** `CutOff` asks the rotator for every member inside its transaction and inserts the ones it can't rotate as `skipped` with their reason at once (the contract inserted them `waiting` and let `advance` skip them in turn), so the page names them from the start and `link.cut_off{servers, skipped}` agrees with the items. `advance` still asks again when an item's turn comes and skips a server that stopped being rotatable meanwhile (tested).
- **Reasons** are stored as `links.ReasonNotInService` ("not in service") and `links.ReasonNothing` ("no rotatable values") and shown through `cutoff.reason.*` ("its template has no rotatable values").
- **Errors.** `links.ErrNoRotator` (→ 404: the routes exist but there is nothing behind them), `links.ErrNotRetryable` (Retry of an item that isn't `failed`, or of a position the latest cut-off doesn't have → 409), `ErrDeleted` (→ 409, plan and start). Retry works on the link's **latest** cut-off.
- **Subscriber.** `subscriptions.cutoff` is registered only when the module has a `Rotator`. It does not `Kick` the workers: it runs before the dispatcher commits, and the 500 ms poll finds the job. `CutOff` and `RetryCutOff` kick after their commit.
- **"One after another"** is proven by each next rotation job being created by (`CreatedBy: event:<id>`) the event that ended the previous one. Their job rows may overlap by milliseconds: the rotation records `server.credentials_rotated` in its last step's transaction, and the dispatcher can queue and start the next server before the worker marks the first job `succeeded`. The first server's rotation is committed by then, so this is still one rotation at a time.
- **Pages.** `GET /links/:id/cutoff` is a page styled as a strength-2 dialog (crumbs, the servers to rotate with their health, Skipped with the reason, Other links "2 other links in 2 subscriptions get new URIs on their next refresh.", the warning, **Cut off** / Cancel); without anything to rotate it says "Nothing to rotate: Cut off only disables the link." and shows no warning. The link page has a **Cut-off** area at the top of its right column (the latest cut-off: "started 14:02 · 3 min ago · admin", per server the state, a **job** link, the error or reason with "still has the old credential", **Retry**); `GET …/cutoff/status` answers the area alone, `no-store`. The alert band's **Cut off Alex…** is a link to the plan page, and its "what" list says "Disables the link and rotates nl-1, de-1, so copied URIs stop working too." (names joined with commas, not "and"). The Actions area has **Cut off…** (danger). Action ids are `cutoff.action` and `cutoff.band.what` because `TestEveryUsedMessageKeyExists` reads `data-action` literals as message keys. CSS: `.row.cutoff`, `.row.cutoff-item` in `app.css`.
- **Test seams.** `substest.New(t, opts...)` now has a fake `Rotator` (`h.Rotator`, `Refuse(id, err)`) unless `substest.NoRotator()`; the harness registers the job type `fake.rotate` under the module name `fake` (no worker runs it unless a test starts the jobs), and `h.Rotated`, `h.RotationFailed` and `h.Feed(event)` hand the subscriber an event inside a `Write`. `substest.WithServers` wires `Rotator: m.Rotator()`. servers: `serverstest.Harness.Unreachable(ip, refused)` makes the harness's `SSH.Dial` refuse an IP (under the harness mutex, so it is safe while workers run).
- **Gateway draft** (uncommitted in `~/projects/sh-main/nginx/conf.d/proxier.conf`): `map $uri $proxier_log { ~^/(s|r|f)/ 0; default 1; }` above the server block and `access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log json if=$proxier_log;` inside it. Checked in a throwaway `nginx:1.27-alpine` container with the same `log_format`: `/s/<token>` was not logged, `/links/1` and `/sx/` were. nginx's error log still names the path of a request that fails at the gateway; `docs/deployment.md` says so.
- **Docs changed:** `credential-rotation.md` (cut-off built: steps 1–4, rules), `link-lifecycle.md` (edge case, `link.cut_off{servers, skipped}`), `modules/servers.md` (Rotator port), `architecture.md` (ports table), `deployment.md` (the gateway's access log), `roadmap.md` (Phase 2 built, what is left), build README (2d done, the Rotator row done). `events.md` already had `link.cut_off{servers, skipped}`; `open-questions.md` is unchanged until the demo answers questions 1 and 2.
